R2 (--n2-equivalence --block-invariance) is NOT covered: it gets its own declaration B with the same construction and margin. CONSTRUCTION. For each gated float site, the gate compares two bf16 geometries A and B, so |A - B| <= (|A_bf16 - f32| + adapter) + (|B_bf16 - f32| + adapter), where adapter = 1e-5 for values and 1e-4 for logits. Each side is measured at the exact positions the site compares, at all positions where measured; the gate oracle side is sampled, so that site takes max(P_all + O_sample, 2 x P_all). (e)'s completed Q is computed through the gate's own decide_roots and backups; its oracle side is taken as 2 x the pricer side (mirror), over the roots whose selection matches between bf16 and f32. (f) is 1-Lipschitz in the leaves and takes the (c) leaf tail. Each field = 1.25 x its largest site tail, rounded up to 2 significant figures: value_bound 1.25 x 0.02538 (R3.c.leaf_value) -> 0.032; turn1_logit_bound 1.25 x 0.5019 (R1.c.t1_own_logits) -> 0.63; root_logit_bound 1.25 x 0.2076 (R3.b.root_peer_logits) -> 0.26; deeper_logit_bound 1.25 x 0.6897 (R3.c.ply2_own_logits) -> 0.87; near_tie_q_bound = 1.25 x max(value tail 0.02538, dQ tail 0.02158) -> 0.032. No in-scope site is unmeasured or withheld. Notes on the table. The depth-2 (c) leaf quantity is leaf_value; raw_head_* checks do not run under the champion. Root priors (root_peer_logits) take root_logit_bound at every site, (b) against all nine lanes of D3's reply logits included. R1 --block-invariance (block_lanes 729 against 2187) is kept: the two programs are bit-identical at both precisions. R3's turn 1 is bit-identical to the depth-2 frame's at both precisions, so its root and turn-1 sites share R1's tails. D3's FramePricer on the saved roots uses actor_capacity 33 (historical window 32), as measured. (e) DQ. R1: max |dQ| 0.0108 over every root (full width: no selection differences); site tail 0.0216. R3: the same-selection dQ is 0.00186, but only 4 of 3769 roots keep an identical selection between bf16 and f32 at k=3, so that tail is thin. The all-roots figure, 0.2099, counts roots where bf16 and f32 chose different children (selection differences: turn 1 4238, ply 2 12538, leaves 214253). (e) never sees those, because it compares a frame against its own oracle-heads copy on the same tree. On the sampled validation rows the pricer's and the oracle's bf16 outputs were bit-identical except at the root, so the gate's dQ is expected near 0. Pre-stated: if R3's clean call FAILs on (e) alone, the result is recorded as FAIL, with the dQ measurement as its diagnostic and no re-verdict. NEAR TIES. At near_tie_q_bound 0.032, 1711 of 3769 R1 roots and 1535 of 3769 R3 roots have a bf16 top-two gap within the bound (top-two gap p10: 0.0051 for R1, 0.0059 for R3). Their flips are reported, not gated. GUARD. GUARD_DECLARED_RULE (fixed by the lead before any champion result) applies: under --declared-bounds the misplacement guard is digest-certified, report-only where the certifying digest check has no mismatch anywhere, values come from one parameter set, and positions outside the digest's mask are bit-equal; otherwise it is gated. depth2_pass_t1_value has no certifying digest and stays gated. Measured, against the guard (0.25 x the p10 non-zero spread): R1 p10 0.117, guard 0.0293; a clean run passes the guard outright at 0.68-0.70 x its bound. R3 p10 0.0335, guard 0.0084; the bf16 tails sit at 2.4-3.0 x the guard, so R3 stays clean only through digest certification. R3's depth2_pass_t1_value reads R1's frame turn 1 against its own; both are bit-identical, at 2.37 x the guard. KILL TEST. --mutation-test needs --depth >= 3, so R3 is a second run under this same declaration. MUTATION_RULE: R3 PASSes iff its clean call passes and stays unchanged, every mutant is exercised and killed (FAIL with a gated check failing other than through a guard alone), and neither seeded sweep has a material survivor. A surviving mutant means these bounds are too loose, and the gate FAILs. That is why value_bound covers depth-3 leaves. EXACT COVERAGE. At depth 2, scatter-path misplacement is caught exactly by (a)'s leaf digests, and backup-path misreads by (f)'s read identity and the exact prior check. The logit bounds guard numeric forward drift only. Prior misreads are caught exactly by (f) and the exact prior check, and adapter correctness by gap 2's f32 match (chunk 0: values 5.2e-7, logits 2.3e-5, against bounds 1e-5 and 1e-4). No mutant tests a logit bound: a known limit, not a hole. Measured, not gated: gap 2's near-terminal check was INCONCLUSIVE (chunk 0 has no unanimous near-terminal parents).
